*Early Life and Accession*

Raymond III was born around 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Hodierna daughter of King Baldwin II of Jerusalem. He inherited the county after his father was assassinated in 1152. At that time he was still a minor and his mother Hodierna acted as regent until he reached maturity. His early years were marked by efforts to stabilize the region amid tensions with neighboring Muslim powers and internal Crusader rivalries. He married Eschiva of Bures who held the title Princess of Galilee thereby uniting the County of Tripoli with the Principality of Galilee. This marriage strengthened his position and gave him claims over Tiberias and surrounding lands. During his youth he also forged alliances with the Knights Templar and the Knights Hospitaller to bolster his defenses. The period saw occasional raids from Nur ad-Din and later from Saladin testing the young count's resolve.

*Reign and Politics*

Raymond III assumed full control of Tripoli in the mid 1150s and quickly became a notable leader among the Crusader nobles. He frequently acted as mediator between the king of Jerusalem and other regional lords seeking to balance royal authority with feudal independence. His relationship with Baldwin IV the Leper King was complex; he respected the king's authority yet often pursued his own agenda especially concerning Galilee and Tiberias. In the 1170s Raymond III opposed the rising influence of Raynald of Châtillon whose provocative actions threatened the fragile truce with Muslim states. He supported the coronation of Baldwin V as co‑king hoping to secure a stable succession. When Baldwin IV died in 1185 Raymond III backed the claim of Sibylla and her husband Guy of Lusignan but soon grew dissatisfied with Guy's leadership. He entered into negotiations with Saladin aiming to protect his territories from outright conquest while preserving Crusader holdings. These diplomatic efforts included offers of tribute and promises of non‑aggression that were viewed with suspicion by hardliners in Jerusalem. Despite his attempts to avoid open conflict Raymond III was drawn into the field army that confronted Saladin at the Battle of Hattin in 1187. His cautious counsel urged a defensive stance but the Crusader command chose to march onto the hot desert plain resulting in a disastrous defeat. After the battle Raymond III retreated to Tripoli where he sought to organize resistance and regroup the remaining forces.
